Admission Plasma Glucose Requirement
data.description: Plasma glucose range required on Day 1 for admission to CRU; otherwise admission is rescheduled
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Hypoglycemia Induction Endpoint (Insulin Infusion Stop)
data.description: Threshold for stopping the IV insulin infusion during the hypoglycemia induction procedure
data.text: Insulin infusion is stopped once bedside PG is <60 mg/dL; approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Hypoglycemia Symptom Assessment Trigger
data.description: PG threshold defining the 'during hypoglycemia induction' assessment time point for the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale
data.text: During hypoglycemia induction will be when PG <=75 mg/dL.

data.name: Insulin Regimen Acceptability
data.description: Review of patient insulin regimen prior to hypoglycemia induction
data.text: Review patients' insulin regimens to confirm acceptability to undergo the procedure to induce hypoglycemia.

data.name: Interim Safety Review After First 6 Patients
data.description: Gating safety review before dosing remaining patients
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients (regardless of type of diabetes) are administered LY900018 in Period 2. The investigator and Lilly CRP or scientist will review available safety data, including AEs, SAEs, vital signs, ECGs, and safety laboratory tests, after these patients complete Period 2 Day 1. If no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure are noted, the remaining patients will be dosed.

data.name: Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration
data.description: Predefined procedures are applied if the patient does not respond sufficiently to glucagon administration
data.text: Procedures for Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration (Section 9.2.4).

data.name: Pre-Discharge Glucose Stability and Meal
data.description: Requirements prior to discharge from the CRU
data.text: After completion of all PK sampling, patients will be provided a carbohydrate-rich meal. The investigator will ensure the patient's PG is stable. A prandial insulin dose will be administered if needed.

data.name: Treatment-Emergent ADA Additional Follow-up Condition
data.description: Condition triggering additional immunogenicity follow-up and its stopping rule
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up. Samples for immunogenicity should be collected every 12 weeks (84+/-7 days) until the titer returns to baseline (ie, returns to within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer) or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Non-Inferiority Success Criterion
data.description: Statistical criterion for declaring non-inferiority of LY900018 versus IMG
data.text: Non-inferiority of LY900018 will be declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI constructed on the difference in percentage (IMG - LY900018) is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%.

data.name: Completer / Sample Size Condition
data.description: Number of evaluable completers required and replacement rules
data.text: Seventy five patients may be enrolled in order to have at least 66 patients (at least 30 patients with T1DM and T2DM, respectively) complete both periods with evaluable primary outcome. If patients discontinue before completion of both periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason, the patient may be replaced. Replacement should not occur beyond 75 patients enrolled.

data.name: Period 2 Procedure Time Matching
data.description: Timing alignment condition between periods
data.text: Procedures in Period 2 will occur at approximately the same time as those in Period 1.

data.name: Predose Assessment Timing Condition
data.description: Definition of the predose time point
data.text: Predose time point will be between insulin infusion stop and study treatment administration.

data.name: Inadvertently Enrolled Patient Continuation Condition
data.description: Condition allowing a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria to remain in the study
data.text: A discussion must occur between the Lilly CP/CRP and the investigator to determine if the patient may continue. If both agree it is medically appropriate, the investigator must obtain documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP to allow the inadvertently enrolled patient to continue in the study with or without continued treatment with investigational product.

data.name: Screening to Period 1 Transition
data.text: Patients undergo screening examination within 28 days prior to enrollment (Days -28 to -2) and must meet eligibility criteria; prior to study drug administration on Period 1 Day 1, patients are randomly assigned to a treatment sequence (LY900018 then IMG, or IMG then LY900018).

data.name: Admission Reschedule for Out-of-Range Plasma Glucose
data.text: Admission to the CRU can be rescheduled if the PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Period 1 to Washout Transition (Discharge)
data.text: Patients remain in the CRU for at least 6 hours after glucagon administration and receive a carbohydrate-rich meal prior to discharge; patients may stay longer as needed at the discretion of the investigator.

data.name: Washout to Period 2 Transition
data.text: Periods 1 and 2 dosing must be separated by a washout period of 3 to 14 days.

data.name: Crossover Treatment Sequence Switch
data.text: Patients receive the alternate treatment in Period 2 per randomized sequence (LY900018 3 mg nasal in one period and IMG 1 mg IM in the other).

data.name: Safety Gate Before Dosing Remaining Patients
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients are administered LY900018 in Period 2 and complete Period 2 Day 1; the remaining patients will be dosed only after confirmation of safety with no clinically significant safety findings.

data.name: Period 2 to Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients will return for a follow-up visit 26 to 30 days (28+/-2 days) after the last study treatment.

data.name: Follow-up to Additional TE ADA Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients with treatment-emergent antidrug antibodies at follow-up/ED will undergo additional immunogenicity follow-up every 12 weeks (84+/-7 days) until titer returns to baseline or until 1 year after the last dose.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop and Dosing Trigger
data.text: The IV insulin infusion will be stopped once bedside PG reaches <60 mg/dL, and approximately 5 minutes later patients will be administered either 3 mg LY900018 or 1 mg IMG.

data.name: Rescue for Insufficient Response to Glucagon
data.text: Procedures for insufficient response to glucagon administration will be followed (Section 9.2.4).

data.name: Rescue with Carbohydrate-Rich Meal and Prandial Insulin
data.text: After completion of all PK sampling, patients will be provided a carbohydrate-rich meal; the investigator will ensure the patient's PG is stable and a prandial insulin dose will be administered if needed.

data.name: Discontinuation for Enrollment in Another Study
data.text: Enrollment in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or in any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

data.name: Discontinuation for Medical, Safety, or Regulatory Reasons
data.text: Participation in the study needs to be stopped for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and good clinical practice.

data.name: Discontinuation by Investigator Decision
data.text: The investigator decides that the patient should be discontinued from the study for any reason. If this decision is made because of an AE, SAE, or a severe hypoglycemia event, appropriate measures are to be taken and Lilly or its designee is to be alerted.

data.name: Discontinuation by Patient Decision
data.text: The patient, or legal representative, requests to be withdrawn from the study.

data.name: Discontinuation of Inadvertently Enrolled Patients
data.text: If a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria was inadvertently enrolled, the patient is discontinued unless the Lilly CP/CRP and investigator agree it is medically appropriate to continue and documented approval is obtained.

data.name: Early Discontinuation (ED) Visit
data.description: Patients discontinuing from the study prematurely for any reason must complete AE and follow-up procedures as shown in the Schedule of Activities; follow-up/ED assessments are performed within 28+/-2 days after the last study treatment.

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome plus the follow-up visit 26 to 30 days after the last study treatment (and any required additional TE ADA follow-up).

data.name: Termination of the Entire Study for Safety
data.description: Following review of safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1, the study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Lost to Follow-up
data.description: A patient will be considered lost to follow-up if he or she repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site, despite diligent attempts by site personnel.

data.name: Exit due to Inadvertent Enrollment (Protocol Deviation)
data.description: A patient identified as not meeting enrollment criteria who was inadvertently enrolled must be discontinued unless documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP is obtained to continue.

data.name: Discharge from CRU After Each Period
data.description: Patient may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration, after all PK sampling and a carbohydrate-rich meal with stable PG; a patient may remain inpatient at the CRU at the discretion of the investigator.

data.name: End of TE ADA Follow-up
data.description: Immunogenicity follow-up ends when the ADA titer returns to within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer or 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Admission Eligibility Decision (Plasma Glucose Check)
data.description: On Day 1 of each period, admission proceeds only if PG is 90 to 250 mg/dL and the insulin regimen is acceptable to undergo hypoglycemia induction; otherwise admission is rescheduled.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop / Dosing Decision
data.description: Once bedside PG is <60 mg/dL the insulin infusion is stopped and study treatment is administered approximately 5 minutes later (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Post-Dose Response Decision
data.description: Assessment of response to glucagon administration; if response is insufficient, Section 9.2.4 rescue procedures are followed. PG stability and meal required before discharge.

data.name: Interim Safety Review Decision After First 6 Patients
data.description: After the first 6 patients complete Period 2 Day 1, the investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist review safety data; the remaining patients are dosed only if no clinically significant safety findings, otherwise the study may be stopped.

data.name: Washout Adequacy Decision
data.description: Period 2 dosing may occur only after a 3 to 14 day washout, with procedures scheduled at approximately the same time of day as Period 1.

data.name: TE ADA Additional Follow-up Decision
data.description: At the follow-up/ED visit, patients with treatment-emergent antidrug antibodies enter additional immunogenicity follow-up every 84+/-7 days until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Primary Non-Inferiority Analysis Decision
data.description: With 66 evaluable completers, non-inferiority is declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI for the difference (IMG - LY900018) is less than the 10% non-inferiority margin.

data.name: Patient Replacement Decision
data.description: If a patient discontinues before completing both periods with evaluable primary outcome, the patient may be replaced, not exceeding 75 patients enrolled.

data.name: Inadvertently Enrolled Patient Continuation Decision
data.description: Joint Lilly CP/CRP and investigator decision, with documented approval, on whether an inadvertently enrolled patient may continue with or without study treatment.
